narrative:
The model estimated your chance of being a bad credit risk at 38.0%. Under the bank’s approval policy, that is above the acceptable risk cutoff, so your application was denied. The single strongest reason was the status of your checking account: it was overdrawn/negative. Among approved applicants, only about 12.6% had a negative checking balance, while 59.2% had no checking account at all, so this stood out as the most influential warning signal and pushed the decision toward bad credit.

The second most important factor was your savings information, recorded as unknown/none. This actually worked in your favor and pushed toward good credit, likely because roughly a third of approved applicants also show no known savings, so it was not treated as a decisive flaw. The third factor was the purpose of the loan, which fell outside the most common categories such as radio/TV or furniture. It also worked slightly in your favor.

Other details, such as requesting 1,358 DM and 24 months, were considered but mattered less than these top three. To improve future chances, reduce or clear the negative checking balance and build a documented savings history. You could also apply for a smaller amount or shorter term, and ask the bank what specific balance or savings level would meet their cutoff. If your circumstances have changed, provide updated bank statements and evidence of stable income.
